plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: In which year was the Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) constituted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)?
plain.explanation: The Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) was constituted by the ICAI on 21st April 1977. Its primary function is to formulate Accounting Standards for Indian entities.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, who prescribes the Accounting Standards for companies in India?
options: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) directly
The Central Government after considering recommendations of National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
plain.explanation: Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 states that the Central Government (Ministry of Corporate Affairs) prescribes the Accounting Standards based on recommendations made by NFRA in consultation with ICAI.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: What is the turnover threshold above which a non-company entity is categorized as a Level I entity as per ICAI guidelines?
options: Exceeding ₹50 crore
Exceeding ₹100 crore
Exceeding ₹250 crore
Exceeding ₹500 crore
plain.explanation: As per the revised criteria issued by ICAI for classification of non-company entities, an entity whose turnover (excluding other income) exceeds ₹250 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year is categorized as Level I.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: What is the maximum borrowing threshold (including public deposits) allowed for a company to qualify as a Small and Medium Company (SMC) under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
options: Does not exceed ₹10 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
Does not exceed ₹25 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
Does not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
Does not exceed ₹100 crore at any time during the preceding accounting year
plain.explanation: Under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021, an SMC's borrowings (including public deposits) must not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Which of the following bodies is responsible for issuing International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)?
options: International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC)
International Accounting Standards Board (IASB)
Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB)
International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)
plain.explanation: The International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), an independent standard-setting body of the IFRS Foundation, formulates and issues IFRS.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: How many levels of classification are specified by ICAI for non-company entities for the applicability of Accounting Standards?
options: Two levels (SMC and Non-SMC)
Three levels (Level I, Level II, Level III)
Four levels (Level I, Level II, Level III, Level IV)
Five levels (Level I to Level V)
plain.explanation: ICAI revised the classification scheme for non-company entities into four distinct levels: Level I (Large), Level II (Medium), Level III (Small), and Level IV (Micro).

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Which of the following statements correctly describes Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)?
options: Ind AS are identical copy-paste versions of US GAAP
Ind AS are Accounting Standards issued directly by ICAI without MCA notification
Ind AS are converged versions of IFRS tailored to the Indian economic and legal environment
Ind AS apply only to sole proprietorships and partnership firms
plain.explanation: Ind AS are Accounting Standards converged with IFRS (incorporating Indian carve-outs/carve-ins) notified by the MCA under the Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: What is the maximum turnover ceiling for a non-company entity to be classified as Level IV (Micro Enterprise)?
options: Up to ₹2 crore
Up to ₹5 crore
Up to ₹10 crore
Up to ₹25 crore
plain.explanation: Level IV non-company entities are those with turnover (excluding other income) not exceeding ₹10 crore in the immediately preceding accounting year and borrowings not exceeding ₹2 crore.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: A company whose equity or debt securities are listed on any recognized stock exchange in India is automatically classified as:
options: A Small and Medium Company (SMC)
A Non-SMC
A Level IV Entity
Exempt from Accounting Standards
plain.explanation: Listed companies or companies in the process of listing cannot qualify as SMCs under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021; they are categorized as Non-SMCs.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Which accounting standard issued by ICAI deals with 'Cash Flow Statements'?
options: AS 1
AS 3
AS 7
AS 10
plain.explanation: AS 3 deals with Cash Flow Statements. Level II, III, and IV non-company entities as well as SMCs are granted certain relaxations/exemptions under this standard depending on statutory provisions.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: When testing the borrowing condition for SMC status of a company for FY 2024-25, during what timeframe must the borrowing limit of ₹50 crore NOT be exceeded?
options: At the end of the current financial year (31st March 2025)
At any time during the immediately preceding financial year (FY 2023-24)
At the end of the immediately preceding financial year (31st March 2024) only
On average basis during the preceding three financial years
plain.explanation: The condition specifies that the borrowings (including public deposits) must not exceed ₹50 crore at any time during the immediately preceding accounting year.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: If an existing Non-SMC entity subsequently satisfies all criteria to become an SMC, for how many consecutive years must it satisfy those criteria before it can avail SMC exemptions?
options: Immediately from the current year
One reporting year
Two consecutive reporting years
Three consecutive reporting years
plain.explanation: An entity that was previously classified as a Non-SMC but subsequently meets SMC criteria must continue to meet those criteria for two consecutive years before it can claim SMC relaxations/exemptions.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Firm Alpha (a partnership firm) has turnover of ₹45 crore and borrowings of ₹12 crore during the preceding accounting year. Under which level of non-company classification does Firm Alpha fall?
options: Level I
Level II
Level III
Level IV
plain.explanation: Level II criteria for non-company entities: Turnover between ₹50 crore and ₹250 crore OR borrowings between ₹10 crore and ₹50 crore. Since borrowings (₹12 crore) exceed ₹10 crore but do not exceed ₹50 crore, Firm Alpha is Level II.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Are non-company entities categorized under Level II exempt from AS 17 (Segment Reporting)?
options: No, AS 17 is fully mandatory for Level II entities
Yes, Level II entities are fully exempt from complying with AS 17
Exempt only if turnover is less than ₹20 crore
Exempt only if permitted by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
plain.explanation: AS 17 (Segment Reporting) is mandatory ONLY for Level I non-company entities. Level II, Level III, and Level IV entities are fully exempt from AS 17.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: An unlisted company has a Net Worth of ₹260 crore as of 31st March 2024. Which accounting framework is mandatorily applicable to this company for FY 2024-25?
options: Accounting Standards (AS) under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) under Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015
IFRS directly as issued by IASB
US GAAP
plain.explanation: Under Phase II of the Ind AS roadmap, all unlisted companies having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more on 31st March of any financial year are mandatorily required to adopt Ind AS from the immediate next financial year.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Which of the following statements regarding the applicability of AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) to Non-Company Entities is CORRECT?
options: Exempt for Level II, Level III, and Level IV entities
Mandatory for Level I, Level II, and Level III entities, but exempt for Level IV entities
Exempt for Level III and Level IV entities only
Mandatory for Level I entities only
plain.explanation: AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) is fully applicable to Level I, Level II, and Level III non-company entities. Only Level IV (Micro) non-company entities are granted full exemption from AS 18.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Which body replaced the National Advisory Committee on Accounting Standards (NACAS) under the Companies Act, 2013?
options: Accounting Standards Board (ASSB)
National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
Financial Reporting Review Board (FRRB)
Quality Review Board (QRB)
plain.explanation: The National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) constituted under Section 132 of the Companies Act, 2013 replaced NACAS to advise the Central Government on accounting standards and oversee audit quality.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: If a company adopting Ind AS has a non-listed subsidiary company with a Net Worth of ₹10 crore, what accounting framework must the subsidiary adopt for its standalone financial statements?
options: Companies (AS) Rules, 2021 as its net worth is below ₹250 crore
Ind AS mandatorily, because its holding company is covered under Ind AS
Option to choose between AS and Ind AS
Level IV Non-company framework
plain.explanation: Once Ind AS becomes applicable to a parent company, it mandatorily applies to all its holding, subsidiary, joint venture, and associate companies, irrespective of their individual net worth.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Which standard setting authority was created in 2021 under the IFRS Foundation to establish comprehensive global baseline standards for ESG / sustainability disclosures?
options: Global Reporting Initiative (GRI)
Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB)
International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB)
Climate Disclosure Standards Board (CDSB)
plain.explanation: The IFRS Foundation announced the creation of the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) at COP26 in November 2021 to issue IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021, if an SMC incurs a total borrowing of ₹55 crore for 3 days during FY 2023-24, how does it affect its classification for FY 2024-25?
options: It remains an SMC as the average borrowing for the year was under ₹50 crore
It becomes a Non-SMC because borrowing exceeded ₹50 crore at any time during the preceding year
It remains an SMC if the excess borrowing was repaid within 7 days
It becomes a Level IV entity
plain.explanation: The criterion explicitly specifies that borrowings must not exceed ₹50 crore *at any time* during the immediately preceding accounting year. Exceeding ₹50 crore even for a single day invalidates SMC status.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Which of the following accounting standards is FULLY EXEMPT for Level III non-company entities?
options: AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories)
AS 10 (Property, Plant and Equipment)
AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations)
AS 13 (Accounting for Investments)
plain.explanation: AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations) is exempt for Level III and Level IV non-company entities. AS 2, AS 10, and AS 13 are mandatory across all levels.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: What happens once an entity adopts Ind AS either voluntarily or mandatorily?
options: It can revert back to Indian AS after 3 years
It can revert back to Indian AS if its net worth falls below ₹250 crore
It cannot revert back to Indian AS (Ind AS adoption is irrevocable)
It can switch back if approved by its shareholders in AGM
plain.explanation: Under the Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015, once a company starts applying Ind AS (whether voluntarily or mandatorily), it must continue to comply with Ind AS for all subsequent financial statements (irrevocable rule).

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Entity B (a non-company entity) has Turnover of ₹80 crore and Borrowings of ₹55 crore during the preceding accounting year. Which level of non-company classification applies to Entity B?
options: Level II, because turnover is less than ₹250 crore
Level I, because borrowings exceed ₹50 crore
Level III, because turnover is between ₹50 and ₹250 crore
Level IV, as it is a non-company entity
plain.explanation: An entity is categorized as Level I if ANY of the Level I thresholds are crossed. Since borrowings (₹55 crore) exceed ₹50 crore, Entity B becomes a Level I entity regardless of its turnover.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: If a Non-SMC company incurs a reduction in borrowings and turnover and now qualifies as an SMC, when can it start benefiting from SMC exemptions under Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
options: In the current year itself if board approval is obtained
Only after meeting the SMC criteria for two consecutive accounting years
Only after getting permission from MCA and NFRA
From the immediate next accounting period following the reduction
plain.explanation: An entity classified as Non-SMC that subsequently meets SMC criteria must satisfy those criteria for two consecutive financial years before it can claim SMC relaxations.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: A sole proprietorship trading concern has Turnover of ₹8 crore and bank borrowings of ₹1.5 crore. It holds a 75% stake in a partnership firm that is classified as a Level I non-company entity. What is the level of the sole proprietorship?
options: Level IV, based on its own turnover and borrowings
Level I, because it is a holding entity of a Level I entity
Level III, because holding entities are downgraded by two levels
Level II, based on consolidated figures
plain.explanation: As per ICAI guidelines, holding entities and subsidiary entities of Level I entities are automatically classified as Level I entities, regardless of their individual standalone turnover or borrowings.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Regarding AS 28 (Impairment of Assets), how are Level IV non-company entities treated compared to Level I entities?
options: Level IV entities are completely exempt from AS 28
AS 28 applies to Level IV entities, but with relaxations in determining value in use (e.g., using reasonable estimates without detailed cash flow projections)
AS 28 applies without any relaxations or exemptions to Level IV entities
AS 28 applies to Level IV entities only if they have international borrowings
plain.explanation: AS 28 applies to Level IV entities, but ICAI grants relaxations regarding the calculation of 'value in use'. Level IV entities can estimate value in use using reasonable surrogates/estimates rather than complex discounted cash flow modeling.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Company K is an unlisted Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) with Net Worth of ₹300 crore as on 31st March 2024. Which accounting framework applies to Company K for FY 2024-25?
options: Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
Ind AS under Phase II of the NBFC Roadmap
RBI Core Accounting Rules exclusively
IFRS direct compliance
plain.explanation: Under the NBFC Ind AS Roadmap, Phase II made Ind AS mandatory for all unlisted NBFCs having a Net Worth of ₹250 crore or more from 1st April 2019 onwards. Thus, Company K (Net Worth ₹300 cr) must follow Ind AS.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: How is 'Net Worth' calculated for determining Ind AS applicability for unlisted companies as per MCA guidelines?
options: Paid-up Equity Share Capital + Reserves out of profits - Accumulated Losses - Deferred Revenue Expenditure - Revaluation Reserves
Paid-up Capital + All Reserves + Revaluation Reserves
Total Assets minus Total External Liabilities including Preference Shares
Paid-up Equity Share Capital + Preference Share Capital + General Reserves + Revaluation Reserves
plain.explanation: Net worth is calculated as per Section 2(57) of Companies Act 2013: aggregate value of paid-up share capital + reserves created out of profits + securities premium - accumulated losses - deferred expenditure - revaluation reserve.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: If a non-company entity moves from Level I to Level IV status due to business downsizing, when can it start availing the full exemptions available to Level IV entities?
options: Immediately in the year of downsizing
After remaining in Level IV for two consecutive reporting periods
After remaining in Level IV for three consecutive reporting periods
Only when certified by the ICAI ASSB
plain.explanation: An entity that drops from a higher level (Level I) to a lower level (Level IV) cannot claim exemptions/relaxations of the lower level until it continues to qualify for the lower level for two consecutive reporting periods.

plain.subject: Accounts
plain.prompt: Where there is a conflict between the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and an Accounting Standard notified under Section 133, which of the two shall prevail?
options: The Accounting Standard notified under Section 133
The provisions of the Companies Act, 2013
The guidance note issued by ASSB
The matter must be referred to the High Court
plain.explanation: Accounting Standards are subservient to statutory legislation. If there is a conflict between the Companies Act, 2013 and an Accounting Standard, statutory law (the Companies Act) prevails.

scenarios.subject: Accounts
scenarios.passage:
Vibrant Threads Ltd is an unlisted public manufacturing company incorporated under the Companies Act, 2013. The company is evaluating its accounting framework compliance for FY 2024-25 under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021.

The relevant financial parameters of Vibrant Threads Ltd for the preceding three financial years are as follows:
- FY 2021-22: Turnover = ₹210 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹35 crore.
- FY 2022-23: Turnover = ₹240 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹48 crore.
- FY 2023-24: Turnover = ₹245 crore; Peak Borrowings = ₹54 crore (for 10 days in Nov 2023 due to temporary working capital loan).

Additionally, Vibrant Threads Ltd holds an 80% equity stake in 'WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd', an unlisted small private company with Turnover of ₹12 crore and Peak Borrowings of ₹3 crore during FY 2023-24. Neither company has listed securities or is in the process of listing.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the classification of Vibrant Threads Ltd for FY 2024-25 under the Companies (AS) Rules, 2021?
options: Small and Medium Company (SMC)
Non-SMC
Level IV Non-company Entity
Ind AS mandatory company
linkedMcqs.explanation: For FY 2024-25, compliance is based on preceding year FY 2023-24 figures. Peak borrowings reached ₹54 crore in FY 2023-24, exceeding the ₹50 crore limit. Hence, Vibrant Threads Ltd is a Non-SMC.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: How does the classification of Vibrant Threads Ltd as a Non-SMC for FY 2024-25 affect its subsidiary 'WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd'?
options: WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd remains an SMC because its own borrowings are only ₹3 crore
WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC because it is a subsidiary of a Non-SMC
WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd is reclassified as a Level IV non-company entity
WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd is exempt from all Accounting Standards
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the definition of SMC in Companies (AS) Rules, 2021, a company that is a subsidiary or holding company of a Non-SMC cannot be treated as an SMC. Thus, WeaveCraft Pvt Ltd becomes a Non-SMC.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Vibrant Threads Ltd repays its loans so that peak borrowing in FY 2024-25 drops to ₹30 crore, in which financial year can it first claim SMC relaxations/exemptions?
options: Immediately in FY 2024-25
linkedMcqs.explanation: A Non-SMC that subsequently meets SMC criteria must meet those criteria for two consecutive reporting periods (FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26) before it can claim SMC exemptions. Thus, it can claim exemptions in FY 2027-28 (based on two consecutive years of compliance).

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Vibrant Threads Ltd required to present a Cash Flow Statement as per AS 3 for FY 2024-25?
options: No, because it is an unlisted company
Yes, because it is classified as a Non-SMC and does not qualify for small company exemption under Section 2(40)
No, because its turnover is less than ₹250 crore
Optional at the discretion of the Board of Directors
linkedMcqs.explanation: Cash Flow Statement (AS 3) is mandatory for Non-SMCs. Exemptions under Section 2(40) apply only to One Person Companies, Small Companies, Dormant Companies, and Startups; Vibrant Threads Ltd does not qualify.

scenarios.subject: Accounts
scenarios.passage:
Apex Consultancy Services is a partnership firm providing IT advisory services in India. The firm's partners are analyzing the applicability of Accounting Standards issued by ICAI for FY 2024-25.

Financial parameters of Apex Consultancy Services for FY 2023-24:
- Turnover (excluding other income): ₹42 crore
- Bank Borrowings (Peak balance): ₹8 crore
- Fixed Deposits accepted from partners/public: ₹3 crore

During FY 2023-24, Apex Consultancy Services acquired a 65% equity stake in 'Global Tech Solutions LLP', a non-company entity with Turnover of ₹280 crore in FY 2023-24.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the non-company classification level of 'Global Tech Solutions LLP' for FY 2024-25?
options: Level I
Level II
Level III
Level IV
linkedMcqs.explanation: Global Tech Solutions LLP has a turnover of ₹280 crore in FY 2023-24, which exceeds the ₹250 crore threshold. Therefore, it is a Level I non-company entity.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the non-company classification level of 'Apex Consultancy Services' for FY 2024-25?
options: Level III, based on its standalone turnover and borrowings
Level II, based on its total borrowings of ₹11 crore
Level I, because it is the holding entity of a Level I entity
Level IV, because it is a partnership firm
linkedMcqs.explanation: Even though Apex's standalone turnover (₹42 cr) and total borrowings (₹11 cr) place it in Level II, holding entities of Level I entities are automatically classified as Level I entities.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Apex Consultancy Services claim exemption from complying with AS 17 (Segment Reporting) for FY 2024-25?
options: Yes, because its turnover is below ₹50 crore
No, because AS 17 is fully mandatory for all Level I entities
Yes, because it is a partnership firm
Yes, if all partners consent unanimously
linkedMcqs.explanation: AS 17 is mandatory for Level I entities. Since Apex Consultancy Services is classified as Level I (due to holding a Level I subsidiary), it cannot claim exemption from AS 17.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Apex Consultancy Services sells its entire stake in Global Tech Solutions LLP during FY 2024-25, when can it start claiming Level III exemptions on a standalone basis (assuming its figures remain Turnover ₹42 cr, Borrowings ₹8 cr)?
options: Immediately in FY 2024-25
From FY 2025-26
Only after remaining in Level III criteria for two consecutive reporting periods
It can never claim Level III exemptions
linkedMcqs.explanation: When an entity drops from Level I to a lower level (Level III), it must continue to meet the criteria of the lower level for two consecutive reporting periods before availing of exemptions.

scenarios.subject: Accounts
scenarios.passage:
Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd is an unlisted private company incorporated in 2015 operating a chain of supermarkets. The company has seen rapid expansion. Its financial position across recent years is summarised below:

- 31st March 2022: Net Worth = ₹190 crore; Turnover = ₹450 crore
- 31st March 2023: Net Worth = ₹240 crore; Turnover = ₹520 crore
- 31st March 2024: Net Worth = ₹270 crore; Turnover = ₹610 crore

Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd has two non-listed subsidiaries: 'Tiny Express Pvt Ltd' (Net Worth ₹12 crore) and 'Fast Logistics Pvt Ltd' (Net Worth ₹8 crore). Neither parent nor subsidiaries are banks, FIs, or NBFCs.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: From which financial year is Ind AS mandatorily applicable to Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd?
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Phase II of the Ind AS roadmap, unlisted companies with Net Worth >= ₹250 crore on 31st March of any FY must adopt Ind AS from the next FY. Net worth reached ₹270 crore on 31st March 2024; hence Ind AS applies from FY 2024-25.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Ind AS applicable to 'Tiny Express Pvt Ltd' for FY 2024-25, despite its Net Worth being only ₹12 crore?
options: No, because its Net Worth is below ₹250 crore
Yes, mandatory because its parent company Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd is adopting Ind AS from FY 2024-25
Optional at the choice of Tiny Express Pvt Ltd's Board
No, unless its turnover exceeds ₹100 crore
linkedMcqs.explanation: Once Ind AS applies to a holding company, it automatically applies to all its holding, subsidiary, joint venture, and associate companies regardless of their individual net worth.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd's Net Worth falls to ₹220 crore on 31st March 2026, can it switch back from Ind AS to Companies (AS) Rules, 2021 for FY 2026-27?
options: Yes, because net worth fell below ₹250 crore
Yes, subject to approval from MCA
No, once Ind AS is applied, the company must continue applying Ind AS indefinitely
Yes, if shareholders pass a special resolution
linkedMcqs.explanation: Ind AS adoption is an irrevocable process. Once a company starts preparing statements under Ind AS, it cannot revert to Accounting Standards (AS) even if its Net Worth drops below the threshold.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: When Nova Retail Services Pvt Ltd prepares its first Ind AS financial statements for FY 2024-25, what comparative information must it present?
options: No comparative figures are required for the first year of adoption
Comparative figures for the preceding year (FY 2023-24) converted to Ind AS
Comparative figures for the last 3 preceding years under Indian AS
Comparative figures under IFRS as issued by IASB
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Ind AS 101 (First-time Adoption of Ind AS), an entity must present at least one year of comparative information under Ind AS (i.e., FY 2023-24 comparative figures translated to Ind AS).

scenarios.subject: Accounts
scenarios.passage:
In 2024, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) examined the standard-setting mechanism in India. A private corporate group, 'GigaTech Enterprises Group', operates multiple legal entities:

1. GigaTech Solutions Ltd (Unlisted Public Co., Turnover ₹300 crore, Net Worth ₹260 crore)
2. GigaTech Softwares Pvt Ltd (Unlisted Co., Turnover ₹40 crore, Net Worth ₹15 crore)
3. GigaTech Hardware LLP (LLP, Turnover ₹8 crore, Borrowings ₹1.2 crore)

The chief accountant is analyzing standard setting authorities, Section 133 of Companies Act 2013, NFRA jurisdiction, and standard classification.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which body formulates Accounting Standards and recommends them to NFRA for consideration before notification by MCA?
options: Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) of ICAI
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Ministry of Finance
linkedMcqs.explanation: The Accounting Standards Board (ASSB) set up by ICAI formulates Accounting Standards and submits them to NFRA. NFRA then examines them and makes recommendations to the Central Government (MCA).

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which set of Accounting Standards applies to 'GigaTech Hardware LLP' for FY 2024-25?
options: Companies (Ind AS) Rules, 2015
Companies (AS) Rules, 2021
Accounting Standards issued by ICAI for Non-Company Entities (Level IV)
IFRS direct framework
linkedMcqs.explanation: GigaTech Hardware LLP is an LLP (non-company entity). Statutory Companies Rules do not apply to LLPs directly. The ICAI issued scheme for Non-Company Entities applies; with Turnover ₹8 cr and Borrowings ₹1.2 cr, it is Level IV.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under Section 134(5)(a) of the Companies Act, 2013, what must Directors state in the Directors' Responsibility Statement regarding Accounting Standards?
options: That Accounting Standards are optional for private companies
That in preparation of annual accounts, applicable accounting standards have been followed along with proper explanation for material departures
That all accounting standards have been relaxed by the statutory auditor
That standards set by FASB US have been complied with
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 134(5)(a) mandates that directors state in the Directors' Responsibility Statement that in the preparation of annual accounts, applicable accounting standards were followed with proper explanation for any material departures.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the relationship between Ind AS and IFRS regarding 'Carve-outs'?
options: Carve-outs are additions made in Ind AS that do not exist in IFRS
Carve-outs are deviations/differences in Ind AS from IFRS to suit Indian legal and economic conditions
Carve-outs represent complete rejection of IFRS principles
Carve-outs apply only to public sector undertakings
linkedMcqs.explanation: Carve-outs refer to departures made in Ind AS from the corresponding IFRS standards to address specific Indian economic, legal, or regulatory circumstances.

scenarios.subject: Accounts
scenarios.passage:
Greenfield Farmers LLP is an agricultural partnership enterprise operating in Punjab. It is not listed and has no financial institutions as partners. 

Financial details for Greenfield Farmers LLP for FY 2023-24:
- Turnover (excluding government grants): ₹7.5 crore
- Bank Borrowings (Peak balance): ₹1.6 crore
- Total Assets: ₹5.0 crore

The management of Greenfield Farmers LLP wants to understand its compliance requirements for FY 2024-25 regarding AS 3 (Cash Flow Statements), AS 17 (Segment Reporting), AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures), and AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations).

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the non-company classification level of Greenfield Farmers LLP for FY 2024-25?
options: Level I
Level II
Level III
Level IV
linkedMcqs.explanation: With turnover up to ₹10 crore (₹7.5 cr) and borrowings up to ₹2 crore (₹1.6 cr), Greenfield Farmers LLP falls under Level IV (Micro non-company entities).

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Which of the following standards is FULLY APPLICABLE to Greenfield Farmers LLP without exemption?
options: AS 3 (Cash Flow Statements)
AS 17 (Segment Reporting)
AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories)
AS 24 (Discontinuing Operations)
linkedMcqs.explanation: AS 2 (Valuation of Inventories) is mandatory for all non-company entities including Level IV. AS 3, AS 17, and AS 24 are exempt for Level IV entities.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Greenfield Farmers LLP required to comply with AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) for FY 2024-25?
options: Yes, AS 18 is mandatory for all entities regardless of level
No, Level IV entities are fully exempt from AS 18
Yes, but with partial disclosures only
Exempt only if turnover is less than ₹1 crore
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under the revised ICAI scheme for non-company entities, AS 18 (Related Party Disclosures) is fully exempt for Level IV entities.

linkedMcqs.subject: Accounts
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Greenfield Farmers LLP takes a new business expansion loan in FY 2024-25 taking peak borrowings to ₹4.0 crore (turnover remaining ₹8.0 cr), what will be its level for FY 2025-26?
